It is proved via eq_top_of_forall_inertia_le (line 212) and Minkowski. The module doc at lines 40–42 calls it the missing input of Mathlib's Morse TODO. At Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Morse.lean lines 28–32 list both TODOs (the number-field specialization via Minkowski, and Gal(X^n − X − 1) = S_n). Its theorem at line 84 takes exactly `hG : ⨆ m : MaximalSpectrum S, m.asIdeal.inertia G = ⊤` (line 87), which Tau Ceti's theorem supplies with S = 𝓞 K. The omission is real, but the fix needs one adjustment. At Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/ConstantField.lean:95 proves `algebraicClosure k F = ⊥ ↔ IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F` (variables at line 56; namespace TauCeti). TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/GeometricDegree.lean:251 `finrank_constantCompositum_eq_finrank_of_isSeparable (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']` gives [F·k' : F] = [k' : k] inside a common extension F'. Its docstring (lines 237–239, 22–25) calls this the degree form of linear disjointness. The BelyiMaps layer 9 stage (§9.1) pins characteristic zero and defines an algebraic Belyi pair as `IsFunctionField k F` with exact constants `IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F`. In characteristic 0, regular (k algebraically closed in F, and F/k separable) is exactly this predicate. The IG.5 Hurwitz target (regular extensions of ℚ(T)) therefore has a usable field-level predicate that the note omits. AUDIT-09 cites neither declaration and never mentions IsIntegrallyClosedIn. Adjustment: the audit's clause is not false. For Spec F → Spec k, Mathlib's GeometricallyIntegral (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Geometrically/Integral.lean:40) is regularity in every characteristic; it just has no bridge to field extensions. The replacement note should keep it in those terms, not as a lesser fallback. It should also say the Tau Ceti theorem gives the degree form [F·k' : F] = [k' : k] of linear disjointness for finite separable constant extensions k'/k. The two citations (fit: related) are right. Status stays absent.

The PolynomialGaloisGroups layer 6 stage has the label table (3T1 C₃, 4T1 C₄, 4T3 D₄, 5T1 C₅, 5T2 D₅), HasGaloisLabel, and classification theorems from discriminant and resolvents in degrees 3 and 4. It also has a sound QuinticCertificate over ℤ, `cert.check f = true → HasGaloisLabel (f over ℚ) cert.label`, whose cyclic and dihedral routes give 5T1 and 5T2, with the worked quintics as acceptance instances. Its README section 'Worked examples, as acceptance tests' (content/tau-ceti/PolynomialGaloisGroups/README.md:1448–1490, for Layers 3, 4 and 6) realizes over ℚ: C₃ (x³ − 3x − 1), C₄ (x⁴+x³+x²+x+1), D₄ (x⁴ − 2), C₅ (x⁵+x⁴−4x³−3x²+3x+1) and D₅ (x⁵ − 5x − 12). IG.4's duplicates list only ProfiniteProPGroups layer 5. IG.6's list PolynomialGaloisGroups layer 9 but not layer 6. The accepted RS-29 does not resolve this. Its IG.4 entry (RS-29.result.json:57) keeps 'cyclic and dihedral realizations' with only ProfiniteProPGroups as supplier. Its IG.6 entry (line 69) imports only PGG layer 9. Tau Ceti f790474 has only the label API (TauCeti/GroupTheory/Perm/TransitiveGroupLabel.lean), with no HasGaloisLabel and no realization over ℚ, so this is a duplicate and not a library claim. Adjustment to the notes: the overlap covers explicit low-degree instances only, not IG.4's general cyclic and dihedral families. Certificates exist only in degree 5. Degrees 3 and 4 have classification theorems (valid over any field of characteristic ≠ 2) plus worked examples. So the IG.6 note should not say 'certificates … for every transitive group of degree ≤ 5'. It should say 'HasGaloisLabel classification in degrees 3–4, sound quintic certificates in degree 5, with worked realizations over ℚ of every transitive group of degree 4 and 5, and of C₃ and S₃'.

The overlap is real mathematically. LV.8 builds the Kodaira–Parshin family and a Hurwitz space, and its requires list has IG.0, IG.1 and IG.3 but not IG.5. But the fix to AUDIT-09 is not the right one, for three reasons. (a) MordellLawrenceVenkatesh is a draft proposed roadmap (research/blueprint/roadmaps/MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.json, status 'draft', review 'needs_changes', 2026-09-24). It is not in data/atlas.json: the string occurs 0 times and there is no extract in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps. The audit's duplicates are scoped to atlas layers (research/blueprint/prompts/AUDIT-09.md:31, 'search the atlas files'), and no accepted audit lists a layer of any of the six new roadmaps. (b) scripts/merge_library_audit.py:57 keeps a duplicates entry only if its layer is a stage of data/atlas.json, so adding LV.8 would be silently dropped from data/library-coverage.json. (c) Under PROTOCOL §15, a proposed roadmap must import what an existing roadmap plans. The defect therefore belongs to the LV draft: LV.8 should cite IG.5 and RP.4's Parshin construction, or a restructuring should settle who owns the Parshin/Kodaira–Parshin construction. The audit of the existing owners IG.5 and RP.4 is not in error. Route this to LV's revision after REV-DESIGN-LV. Also, LV.8's Hurwitz space (covers of a fixed genus-g curve with one moving branch point) is not plainly a case of IG.5's Hurwitz moduli, which are aimed at regular realizations over P^1. Coordinator decision, for consistency with findings 7 and 8: the duplication is real, so the finding is confirmed, but the fix is redirected. MordellLawrenceVenkatesh is a draft roadmap outside data/atlas.json, and scripts/merge_library_audit.py:57 drops duplicates entries whose layer is not an atlas stage, so an entry in AUDIT-09 would never take effect. The fix belongs in the draft roadmap (research/blueprint/roadmaps/MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.json): LV.8 should import IG.5's Hurwitz moduli and descent (add IG.5 to its requires) rather than rebuild them, as PROTOCOL §15 requires.

The CM.1 note on the 'Action of an invertible prime ideal…' target says 'End without zero divisors' and cites TauCeti.Isogeny.Hom.instNontrivialEnd (Hom/Basic.lean:350). That instance proves only Nontrivial; its docstring is 'The carrier has more than one element'. The zero-divisor fact is TauCeti.Isogeny.Hom.comp_eq_zero_iff (Basic.lean:258, 'g.comp f = 0 ↔ g = 0 ∨ f = 0'), made into the anonymous NoZeroDivisors instance at Basic.lean:336. The note's 'additive Hom group' is right (Add.lean:204), but End is not a ring (see /1). The fix is right: cite comp_eq_zero_iff at line 258 with fit related, and append that End(E) is a monoid with zero and an additive group, not yet a ring (only Hom.add_comp).

In RP.1, the target 'An elliptic 2-descent with local conditions and global image…' is marked partial. Yet both declarations carry fit 'exact': pow_rank_le_card_of_range_μ_le (MordellWeil/SelmerGroup.lean:142) and card_range_μ (:128). Those are general lemmas: the bound 2^rank·#E(K)[2] ≤ #S for an arbitrary finite S ⊇ im μ, and #im μ = 2^rank·#E(K)[2]. SelmerGroup.lean:25 says 'Nothing here establishes that the Selmer group is finite', and :139-140 say the lemma applies to selmerGroup₂ only 'once that group is known to be finite'. The stage's acceptance (atlas RP.1) asks for a worked 2-descent example with local conditions, the global image and a finite-generation conclusion, and no such example exists. So 'exact' is wrong. The right label for this target is 'related', not 'special case'. ED.3 uses 'special case' because its target is the general bound ('The rank upper bound from a finite group containing the descent image'), of which these lemmas are the n = 2 case. RP.1's target is a worked example, and a general lemma is not a special case of an example. Change both fits to 'related'. Status stays partial.

Checked MordellWeil/FinitelyGenerated.lean at f790474. fg_point (:90-94) assumes the section variables [AdmissibleAbsValues F] [Northcott (logHeight₁ (K := F))] [DecidableEq F] [IsElliptic] (:66-67). It also takes a Dedekind domain R with fraction field F, [W.IsCharNeTwoNF] (the normal form y² = f(x)), and, for each factor p of W.f, Finite (ClassGroup (W.ringOfIntegersFactor R p)) and Monoid.FG (W.ringOfIntegersFactor R p)ˣ. Verified at the pinned commits. Mathlib 082e2d3 Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean:660-661 reads '/-- The scheme-theoretic image of a morphism. -/ abbrev Hom.image : Scheme.{u} := f.ker.subscheme'. The same file has Hom.toImage_imageι and 'instance [QuasiCompact f] : IsDominant f.toImage'. The scheme-theoretic closure of G_K in a model is the image of G_K -> A, so R28.3's note overstates when it says 'no scheme-theoretic closure of subgroup schemes in integral models exist[s]'. Nothing proves that the closure is a finite flat subgroup scheme, and there are no l-divisible groups or Neron models. The proposed citation (index line 661), the reworded note and the unchanged 'absent' status are all correct.

Verified in Tau Ceti f790474. TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SInteger/SelmerGroup/NumberField.lean:44 has 'theorem finite_selmerGroup_of_numberField [NeZero n] (hS : S.Finite) : Finite (selmerGroup (R := 𝓞 F) (K := F) (S := S) (n := n))' (index line 44), and weak Mordell-Weil uses it (MordellWeil/WeakMordellWeil.lean:21, :97). At Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/ClassSum/StructureConstants.lean:62–69 defines structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ = #{(x,y) ∈ Cᵢ × Cⱼ : xy = g} for any g ∈ Cₖ (structureConstant_mk, line 73). Then #{(x,y,z) ∈ Cᵢ×Cⱼ×Cₖ : xyz = 1} = |Cₖ⁻¹| · structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ⁻¹ = |Cₖ| · structureConstant Cᵢ Cⱼ Cₖ⁻¹, one line from the definition. So the IG.3 note's 'the count of triples with product one … absent' overstates what is missing. What is absent is the character formula for it, generating triples, rigidity and rationality. Correction to the fix: TauCeti.structureConstant is already cited on this very target (AUDIT-09 IG.3, rigidity target: StructureConstants.lean:64, fit related). The 'Add' step is a no-op, and the RT report is wrong to list it as uncited. Only the note text should change, as the finding proposes. Low severity.

Applied to ℤ this is Ẑ as a profinite group, though no named Ẑ or ring structure exists. So 'no Ẑ' in the IG.0 G_m note is imprecise. The accepted RS-06 (data/restructure/RS-06.result.json) narrows R28.2 to the arithmetic determinant/height calculation, with suppliedBy R35.4, R07.1, R06.6 and R34.2. The same result makes R35.4 the owner of the 'Isogeny-height change formula ... with integral differential term'. The accepted RS-02 makes 7E the owner of the elliptic p-divisible tower and narrows R07.1 to import 7E PD-1. So 7E reaches R28.2 as a supplier through R07.1, which the audit already lists; it is not a duplicate. T0 says 'Use the Barsotti-Tate group ... of R07.1-R07.2 ... do not define a second p-divisible group'. Its differential work (the Hodge ideal and the Hodge-Tate map for canonical subgroups) is a different target from R35.4's height term. Adding either entry would record false duplicates. It is true that ModularCurves 7E (PD-2) names EllipticCurve.IsSupersingular via connectedness of E[p], and that PD-4 and PD-5 treat the supersingular and ordinary p-divisible groups. But 7E does not state CM.5's target, which is isogeny graphs of CM curves at good primes; CM.5 only consumes the dichotomy. The audit already lists the owner of that dichotomy, EllipticCurves Layer 3, which defines IsSupersingular and IsOrdinary geometrically over any field of characteristic p. The double definition between 7E and EllipticCurves Layer 3 is already recorded where it belongs: accepted AUDIT-12's entry for tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#7e-p-divisible-groups lists EllipticCurves Layer 3 as a duplicate ('PD-2's dichotomy is the scheme-theoretic definition of the same notion'). It lies between two Tau Ceti roadmaps, which PROTOCOL §15 says are never re-planned here. So the proposed note's 'must agree on one predicate' cannot be acted on in CM.5, and the entry would change nothing about what CM.5 builds.

CM.4's duplicates already name the owners of infinity types and conductors of algebraic Hecke characters: tauceti GlobalNumberFields Layer 10 (infinity types, type A₀ characters) and Layer 9 (Hecke characters with conductors).
